subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should fenced legacy `MEDIA:` directives stay non-extracting with delivery-boundary warnings, be extracted as attachments, or remain a documented by-design constraint only?
rationale: Current code intentionally preserves fenced examples as text, but the issue reports a real silent media-delivery failure; extraction versus diagnostics changes the product contract and false-positive behavior.

options.title: Warn At Delivery Boundary
options.body: Keep fenced tokens as text, emit one warning only when an outbound delivery payload would otherwise silently skip the media, and finish review of the linked PR.

options.title: Extract Standalone Fenced Tokens
options.body: Treat standalone fenced `MEDIA:` lines as attachments, accepting that code examples can become deliverable media unless a stricter policy is designed.

options.title: Docs And Prompt Only
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and rely on docs plus system prompt wording that legacy `MEDIA:` lines must be standalone plain text.

recommendation.title: Warn At Delivery Boundary
recommendation.body: Keep fenced tokens as text, emit one warning only when an outbound delivery payload would otherwise silently skip the media, and finish review of the linked PR.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed the linked PR at the exact warning-boundary decision point.
